chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Faḍl ibn Yūnus al-Kātib, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام and said to him: What is your view regarding a man from among our companions who dies and does not leave behind what he may be shrouded with? Should I buy his shroud for him from the zakat? He said: “Give his dependents from the zakat an amount by which they may prepare him, so that they are the ones who prepare him.”

I said: If he has no child and no one to take charge of his affair, then may I prepare him myself from the zakat? He said: “My father used to say: ‘Indeed, the sanctity of the body of the believer when dead is like its sanctity when alive.’ So cover his body and his private parts, prepare him, shroud him, apply ḥanūṭ to him, count that from the zakat, and accompany his funeral.”

I said: If some of his brothers contribute on his behalf another shroud, while he has a debt upon him, should he be shrouded with one and his debt be paid with the other? He said: “No. This is not an inheritance that he left behind. Rather, this is something that came to him after his death. So let them shroud him with that which was contributed on his behalf, and the other shall be for them, with which they may set right their affair.”

key_terms.بَدَنِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِ: the body of the believer, whose dignity remains after death
key_terms.حُرْمَةَ: the sanctity and inviolability due to the believer
key_terms.مِيرَاثًا: inheritance, which this posthumously acquired item is not
key_terms.ٱلزَّكَاةِ: zakat funds used here for the preparation of a deceased needy believer

ai.seo_question: Can zakat be used to buy a shroud and prepare a deceased believer for burial?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings concerning preparing a deceased believer who has left no means for burial and shrouding. It permits using zakat for funeral preparation, emphasizes the sanctity of the believer’s body after death, and clarifies that goods provided after death are not treated as inheritance for settling debts.
